title: Graph Valid Tree
statement:
You're given `n` nodes labeled 0 to n - 1 and a list of undirected edges, where `[a, b]` connects nodes `a` and `b`. Return `True` if these edges form a single tree, and `False` otherwise.

A tree is connected (every node can reach every other node) and has no cycles. No edge is listed twice, and no edge connects a node to itself.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 2000; 0 <= len(edges) <= 5000; 0 <= a, b < n.
signature: def valid_tree(n: int, edges: List[List[int]]) -> bool:

examples.explanation: Node 1 connects to the other three, and there are no loops.
The three edges make a loop: 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0.
Nothing links {0, 1} to {2, 3}, so the graph is in two pieces.

hints: A tree on n nodes has a very specific number of edges. What is it, and is that count enough on its own?
Look at n = 4 with edges [[0, 1], [1, 2], [2, 0]]: the count is right, so what else has gone wrong?
With exactly n - 1 edges, you only need to rule out one of the two problems, because the other then follows. Which is easier to check?
As you add edges one at a time, how can you tell that an edge joins two nodes that are already connected?
Return False unless there are n - 1 edges, then either union-find each edge (a shared root means a cycle) or run one BFS/DFS from node 0 and check that it reaches all n nodes.
followUps: Why are n - 1 edges and no cycle enough to prove the graph is connected?
What does union-find cost with path compression and union by rank, compared with BFS?
How would you detect a cycle in an undirected graph with DFS without counting the edge back to the parent?
How would you answer this if edges arrived one at a time and you had to report after each one?
idealAnswerPoints: Checks for exactly n - 1 edges up front
Detects a cycle with union-find, or confirms connectivity with one traversal
Explains why the edge count plus one of the two checks is enough
Treats n = 1 with no edges as a valid tree
States O(n + e) time and O(n) space
weakAnswerSigns: Only checks connectivity and misses a cycle when there are extra edges
Treats the edge back to the parent as a cycle in DFS

rubric.correctness: Rejects cycles, disconnected graphs and the right-count-wrong-shape case, and accepts a single node.
rubric.efficiency: O(n + e) with one traversal or near-linear union-find; no repeated searches per edge.
rubric.code_quality: An early edge-count check, then a small find helper or a single BFS over an adjacency list built once.
rubric.communication: States both tree conditions, and why n - 1 edges halves the work, before coding.
